entry.title: Innovation & Impact Podcast: Garrett Reisman’s Journey from Penn to Space

media:group.media:title: Innovation & Impact Podcast: Garrett Reisman’s Journey from Penn to Space
media:group.media:description:
This episode of Penn Engineering’s Innovation & Impact podcast features Penn alum Garrett Reisman, a NASA astronaut, former SpaceX executive and current Professor of Astronautics Practice at the University of Southern California’s Viterbi School of Engineering. After graduating from Penn Engineering through the Jerome Fisher Program in Management & Technology, Reisman earned a Ph.D. from Caltech. During his time with NASA, he flew on three space shuttle missions and spent nearly 100 days aboard the International Space Station. He then went on to help shape SpaceX’s approach to human spaceflight and continues to advise the commercial space sector.
In this episode, host Vijay Kumar, Nemirovsky Family Dean of Penn Engineering and Professor in Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics, joins Reisman in a discussion that explores how the culture and technology of spaceflight have evolved from NASA’s early missions to today’s commercial space industry. Reisman discusses what enabled SpaceX to move quickly, the role of ambitious missions in driving innovation and the balance between experimentation and safety when human lives are at stake.

media:group.media:description:
Spend a day with McKenzie Tebo (ENG’26, GEng’28), a Penn Engineering student, National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) member and dancer.
From classes and lunch with friends to an evening at NSBE’s general body meeting, McKenzie shares a look at the people, activities and communities that make up her day on campus. media:group.media:description:
The Penn Engineering Career Development Hub provides specialized career support for on-campus master’s students.

entry.title: Innovation & Impact Episode 14: "The Future of Data Centers with Ben Lee" | Penn Engineering

media:group.media:title: Innovation & Impact Episode 14: "The Future of Data Centers with Ben Lee" | Penn Engineering
media:group.media:description:
Penn Engineering’s Innovation & Impact podcast features Benjamin Lee, Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering and Computer and Information Science at Penn Engineering and a visiting researcher at Google. Lee’s research explores computer architecture, microprocessors, memory systems and data centers, with a focus on energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.
In this episode, host Vijay Kumar, Nemirovsky Family Dean of Penn Engineering and Professor in Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics, speaks with Lee to examine the growing physical and environmental costs of artificial intelligence, from the electricity and water required to run data centers to the hardware that powers increasingly complex AI models. The conversation explores how advances in chip design, computing architectures and data center operations could make AI more efficient, as well as the challenges of keeping resource consumption in check as demand accelerates.

entry.title: What is Materials Science and Engineering? | Penn Engineering

media:group.media:title: What is Materials Science and Engineering? | Penn Engineering
media:group.media:description:
Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) transforms how we understand, design, and apply materials to solve today’s most pressing challenges. From nanotechnology to sustainable materials, the MSE program at the University of Pennsylvania equips students with the skills and knowledge to engineer the building blocks of innovation.
MSE students and researchers pioneer breakthroughs that fuel innovation, from next-generation batteries to lightweight aerospace materials and biocompatible implants. Our discoveries not only reshape industries but also improve lives and build a more sustainable future.
With access to world-class facilities, interdisciplinary projects, and industry partnerships, students are empowered to lead and innovate. At Penn, the opportunities to explore, create, and make a lasting impact are as limitless as your ambition.

entry.title: Innovation & Impact Episode 13: "The Future of Reasoning with Byron Cook" | Penn Engineering

media:group.media:title: Innovation & Impact Episode 13: "The Future of Reasoning with Byron Cook" | Penn Engineering
media:group.media:description:
On this episode, Dean Vijay Kumar is joined by Byron Cook, Vice President and Distinguished Scientist of the Automated Reasoning Group at Amazon Web Services and Professor at University College London. Cook is a computer scientist and pioneer in automated reasoning whose work sits at the intersection of theory, software and artificial intelligence.
Their conversation examines the evolving relationship between people and intelligent machines, from the challenges of ensuring that increasingly autonomous systems behave as intended to the ways AI is changing software development and problem-solving. Cook also reflects on how research evolves alongside technology and why connecting fundamental ideas with real-world problems can lead to unexpected discoveries.
